headline: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan assaulted in Italy by expatriate Bangladeshis
summary: The actress alleged that members of the Venice Awami League and Chhatra League attacked her for supporting the July uprising.
details: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan was physically assaulted and harassed in Venice, Italy, on Monday, September 7.
Badhan stated in a Facebook Live session that she was visiting a park with her brother's family when a group of expatriate Bangladeshis attacked her.
She alleged that the attackers physically harassed her, snatched her phone and threw it away, and struck her near the ear.
The actress claimed that the attackers identified themselves as members of the Venice Awami League and Chhatra League, targeting her for her support of the July uprising.
Film director Mostofa Sarwar Farooki expressed strong condemnation of the attack, calling for an end to the 'soft power' of fascism within the government.
Farooki urged the interim government to investigate who is empowering fascist elements and ensure that intellectual criminals are held accountable.
Badhan has stated that she remains courageous and will not be intimidated by such acts of violence.
The Milan Consulate has reportedly pledged to provide all necessary assistance to the actress following the incident.
caption:
Physically assaulted, phone snatched, and targeted for her political views—actress Azmeri Haque Badhan was attacked in Italy.

Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan was physically assaulted and harassed in Venice, Italy, on Monday, September 7.

Badhan stated in a Facebook Live session that she was visiting a park with her brother's family when a group of expatriate Bangladeshis attacked her.

She alleged that the attackers physically harassed her, snatched her phone and threw it away, and struck her near the ear.

The actress claimed that the attackers identified themselves as members of the Venice Awami League and Chhatra League, targeting her for her support of the July uprising.

Film director Mostofa Sarwar Farooki expressed strong condemnation of the attack, calling for an end to the 'soft power' of fascism within the government.

Farooki urged the interim government to investigate who is empowering fascist elements and ensure that intellectual criminals are held accountable.

Badhan has stated that she remains courageous and will not be intimidated by such acts of violence.

The Milan Consulate has reportedly pledged to provide all necessary assistance to the actress following the incident.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

topic: govt wants hasina back from india
headline_marked: Govt wants to [[bring Sheikh Hasina back]] to Bangladesh, not wait for return
headline: Govt wants to bring Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh, not wait for return
summary: Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman says the government intends to capture her through legal means as she faces death penalty sentences.
details: Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government wants to bring ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh rather than waiting for her to return voluntarily.
He clarified that the demand for her extradition is not a tactic to pressure India, but a legal necessity as she is an accused, absconding person, and convicted person sentenced to death.
Zahed Ur Rahman added that even if she returns, she will not have the opportunity to seek a review of the trial held against her, as the death penalty awaits her.
The adviser also expressed dissatisfaction over Hasina being allowed to give interviews to Indian media despite Bangladesh's objections.
He stated that Bangladesh expects the Indian government to prevent her from engaging in such activities until her extradition.
India could improve relations by returning Hasina to Bangladesh, according to the adviser.
During the same press conference, the adviser presented data on load-shedding, noting a sharp rise in average daily load-shedding in August 2024 compared to 2023.
He also mentioned that legal proceedings have begun regarding the reported attack on actress Azmeri Haque Badhon in Italy, with the government promising stern action.
caption:
The government will not wait for Sheikh Hasina to return voluntarily; they want to bring her back by capturing her.

Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government wants to bring ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh rather than waiting for her to return voluntarily.

He clarified that the demand for her extradition is not a tactic to pressure India, but a legal necessity as she is an accused, absconding person, and convicted person sentenced to death.

Zahed Ur Rahman added that even if she returns, she will not have the opportunity to seek a review of the trial held against her, as the death penalty awaits her.

The adviser also expressed dissatisfaction over Hasina being allowed to give interviews to Indian media despite Bangladesh's objections.

He stated that Bangladesh expects the Indian government to prevent her from engaging in such activities until her extradition.

India could improve relations by returning Hasina to Bangladesh, according to the adviser.

During the same press conference, the adviser presented data on load-shedding, noting a sharp rise in average daily load-shedding in August 2024 compared to 2023.

He also mentioned that legal proceedings have begun regarding the reported attack on actress Azmeri Haque Badhon in Italy, with the government promising stern action.
